You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: continual-arc-interaction
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; choose a submission or demo request under per-instance scoring.
---

# Continual ARC interaction

1. Parse the current instance's grid, all demo pairs, and remaining attempt/demo budgets; infer a candidate input-output rule. Treat each new instance as fresh unless the task provides reusable context.
2. Before submitting, apply the candidate rule to every demonstrated input and check that it reproduces each demonstrated output cell-for-cell. If any example disagrees, revise the rule or request a demo rather than spending a guess on the test. Submit only when the rule passes this check and yields a complete grid. Account for wrong submissions and demo requests equally in the stated score, and remember an unsolved instance incurs the full stated budget.
3. Return the action as the final line in the exact required JSON shape (`submit` with `grid`, `request_demos`, or `finish`). Do not include extra tool calls or explanatory text when the task requires only the action JSON.
4. After demo feedback, compare input and output cell-by-cell to identify the transformation; after submission feedback, revise the hypothesis rather than repeating the same unsupported guess. Continue with one valid action. Use `finish` only when the instance is over and the task allows it.
